thread.title: S&P 500, Dow Lower, But Nasdaq Climbs As Big Moves Shake This Sector

author: EdJenner
title: S&P 500, Dow Lower, But Nasdaq Climbs As Big Moves Shake This Sector
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average and S&P 500 paused from a string of new highs Thursday, but the Nasdaq composite climbed thanks to technology stocks.
X
The Dow and S&P 500 were on track to end four-day win streaks that included record highs the past three days on the S&P 500. The S&P 500 was down 0.1% after coming off session lows. The Dow Jones industrial average lost 0.2%, with 23 of the 30 components lower.
But the Nasdaq climbed 0.3% and was attempting to stretch its win streak to five sessions. The composite made a new high and traded at session highs in early afternoon. Gains in internet, biotech and some software industry groups helped the Nasdaq hold up better than the other indexes.
The small-cap Russell 2000 was up 0.2% and also on pace to extend a four-day win streak. The index hit a record high Monday.
Volume was tracking higher compared with the same time Wednesday.
Apple ( AAPL ), the largest stock by market capitalization, rose after the company announced a Sept. 12 event . Apple didn’t offer specifics but it’s likely when the company will reveal its latest iPhones and other product updates. Shares hit a new high and are extended from a breakout past a 194.30 buy point.
The retail sector had many stocks making sharp moves after earnings reports.
Guess ( GES ) surged past the 26.25 buy point of a cup without handle, but reversed back into the base. The company beat profit expectations late Wednesday.
Abercrombie & Fitch ( ANF ) plummeted 17% in big volume, falling below the 50-day and 200-day moving averages. The apparel chain posted a surprise profit for the May-July quarter but missed sales expectations and gave a weak outlook.
Signet Jewelers ( SIG ) soared 25% after the company’s July-quarter earnings breezed past expectations , while revenue and same-store sales were surprisingly higher. Signet shares climbed to the highest level since Nov. 20, when another earnings report sparked a long correction.
Other key retailers are reporting earnings after today’s close, including Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ) and Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ). Lululemon is a longtime member of IBD Leaderboard .
Gaming software was one of the poorest industry groups after Electronic Arts ( EA ) tumbled 10% to a nearly four-month low. The company said it is delaying the launch of its new “Battlefield” video game to make some final adjustments. The delay caused Electronic Arts to cut its annual sales forecast.
Karyopharm Therapeutics ( KPTI ) broke out of an undefined base, clearing a 20.49 buy point in heavy trading.
